title: Angles: Parallel Lines, Transversals and Triangles
seo_title: Grade 8 Parallel Lines and Transversals Worksheets: Angle Pairs, Triangle Sum, Exterior Angles
standard_text: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 angle worksheets: corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior and same-side interior angles with parallel lines, the triangle angle sum, exterior angles, and angle equations. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: With parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal; same-side interior angles add to 180°.
key_sub: A triangle's angles add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the two far interior angles added.
body_html:
Parallel lines and a transversal

PairExampleRule
Corresponding∠1 and ∠5equal
Alternate interior∠3 and ∠6equal
Alternate exterior∠1 and ∠8equal
Same-side interior∠3 and ∠5add to 180°
Vertical∠1 and ∠4equal
Linear pair∠1 and ∠2add to 180°

Triangles

The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. An exterior angle equals the sum of the two far interior angles.

Example

In a triangle, two angles are 50° and 65°. Find the third.

180 − 50 − 65 = 65.

Answer: 65°

Common mistakes

  • Subtracting from 180° when the angles are equal (corresponding, alternate).
  • Saying same-side interior angles are equal. They add to 180°.
  • Using 360° for a triangle. The angles add to 180°.

faq.q: Which angles are equal when parallel lines are cut by a transversal?
faq.a: Corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, alternate exterior angles and vertical angles are equal.
Same-side interior angles and any two angles that form a straight line (a linear pair).

faq.q: What is the exterior angle theorem?
faq.a: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it.

faq.q: Why do the angles of a triangle add to 180°?
faq.a: Draw a line through one corner parallel to the opposite side. The three angles of the triangle line up along that straight line, which is 180°.

items.q: ∠1 = 115° and the lines are parallel. Ana says ∠5 = 65°. What did she do wrong?
items.e: Corresponding angles are equal, so ∠5 = 115°. ∠1 and ∠5 are equal, not supplementary.

items.q: A triangle has angles 40° and 60°. Ben says the third angle is 260°. What did he use?
items.e: 360 − 100 = 260. A triangle uses 180°: the third angle is 80°. 360° instead of 180°.

items.q: If same-side interior angles are 75° and 105°, are the lines parallel?
items.e: 75 + 105 = 180, so yes, they add to 180°.

items.q: If corresponding angles are 70° and 75°, are the lines parallel?
c: No, they would have to be equal
items.e: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal: no, they would have to be equal.

items.e: They form a straight line: 180 − 135 = 45°.

items.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is the largest angle?
items.e: x + 2x + 3x = 180, so x = 30 and the largest is 3 × 30 = 90°.

items.q: The sum of the exterior angles of a triangle (one at each corner) is …
items.e: Each exterior angle + interior angle = 180°; three of them = 540°, minus the 180° inside = 360°.

items.q: Which pair of angles is always supplementary?
items.e: Angles on a straight line add to 180°: a linear pair.

items.q: Which pair of angles is equal even if the lines are NOT parallel?
items.e: Vertical angles are always equal.
